title: Store lifecycle emits structured events on a single sink
asA: operator who needs to answer 'when did the store come up, what version did it migrate through, when did the last snapshot land' from the log stream
iWant: the store to emit structured events at open, at every migration run that applied work, at every backup checkpoint, and at close
soThat: the store's lifecycle is a first-class observable and my dashboards do not have to shell into the database to answer basic questions

acceptanceCriteria.description: The store facade accepts an onEvent sink function at open time and invokes it with a structured record on every lifecycle moment: opened at successful open, migrated when the runner applied at least one migration, backupCheckpoint when a snapshot completes, closed on graceful shutdown.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the store is opened with an injected onEvent sink and taken through open, migrate, backup, and close
acceptanceCriteria.when: the sink is inspected after each lifecycle moment
acceptanceCriteria.then: the sink has received one record for each moment with the event name field set to opened, migrated, backupCheckpoint, and closed respectively, each carrying a valid ISO-8601 timestamp

acceptanceCriteria.description: The migrated event carries the schema version transition and the list of migration versions applied during that run.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the store opens against a file at version v_k with the build at max known version v_n where v_n > v_k
acceptanceCriteria.then: the event record contains a from field equal to v_k, a to field equal to v_n, and an applied field whose value is the array of integers v_k+1 through v_n in ascending order

acceptanceCriteria.description: The opened event carries the store identifier the facade was opened against; the backupCheckpoint event carries the artifact path the backup runner wrote to.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the store is opened against identifier I and a subsequent backup writes to artifact path B
acceptanceCriteria.when: the opened and backupCheckpoint events fire
acceptanceCriteria.then: the opened event's store identifier field equals I and the backupCheckpoint event's artifact path field equals B, both as strings the operator can pass back into their tooling verbatim
